pr.title: When deduplicating unreachable blocks, erase the source information.
pr.description:
After deduplication the block conceptually belongs to multiple locations in the source. Although these blocks are unreachable, in #123341 we did come across a real side effect, an unreachable block that survives into the compiled code can cause a debugger to set a breakpoint on the wrong instruction. Erasing the source information ensures that a debugger will never be misled into thinking that the unreachable block is worth setting a breakpoint on, especially after #128627.

Technically we don't need to erase the source information if all the deduplicated blocks have identical source information, but tracking that seems like more effort than it's worth.

pr.author: khuey

analysis.summary: SimplifyCfg's unreachable-block deduplication must erase the surviving block's terminator source information, because a deduplicated block represents multiple source locations. The historical bug kept the first unreachable block's original span/scope, allowing debuggers to map breakpoints to the wrong instruction. The fix sets the kept terminator's SourceInfo to DUMMY_SP and OUTERMOST_SOURCE_SCOPE whenever at least one unreachable block was deduplicated.
analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/simplify.rs`, `remove_dead_blocks` retains one unreachable block and deduplicates later unreachable blocks by recording a replacement: `let kept_unreachable = *kept_unreachable.get_or_insert(used_bb); if kept_unreachable != used_bb { replacements[orig_index] = kept_unreachable; orig_index += 1; return false; }`. Before the fix, the surviving kept block's terminator source information was left untouched.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, when a later unreachable block was deduplicated into the first kept unreachable block (`kept_unreachable != used_bb`), the kept block's terminator retained its own original `SourceInfo` (span and scope). That falsely attributed the merged unreachable code to one source location. As the PR states, "After deduplication the block conceptually belongs to multiple locations in the source." and "an unreachable block that survives into the compiled code can cause a debugger to set a breakpoint on the wrong instruction." The corrected transformation tracks `deduplicated_unreachable` and, only if that flag is set, rewrites the kept block's terminator source info to `SourceInfo { span: DUMMY_SP, scope: OUTERMOST_SOURCE_SCOPE }`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by `SimplifyCfg::remove_dead_blocks` that contain unreachable basic blocks and in which at least two unreachable blocks are recognized as duplicates, causing `kept_unreachable != used_bb` and setting `deduplicated_unreachable`. The two test inputs should differ only in whether such deduplication occurs (or in the source spans of the duplicate unreachable blocks): one with a single/non-deduplicated unreachable block, one with multiple deduplicated unreachable blocks carrying distinct source information.
analysis.trigger: The deduplication branch in `remove_dead_blocks` is taken: a second or later unreachable block is removed and replaced by the already-kept unreachable block, making `kept_unreachable != used_bb` true and setting `deduplicated_unreachable = true`.
preconditions: `remove_dead_blocks` is invoked as part of `SimplifyCfg` on a MIR body with unreachable basic blocks.
More than one unreachable block reaches the deduplication logic such that one is kept and another is replaced with it.
The deduplicated unreachable block can survive into compiled code/debug info, making its source mapping observable to a debugger.
pitfalls: Do not erase source information for all unreachable blocks: the fix applies only when `deduplicated_unreachable` is true.
Do not conflate this with SimplifyLocals; the changed code is the `SimplifyCfg`/`remove_dead_blocks` path.

The PR deliberately erases source info even if all deduplicated blocks happen to share identical source info: "Technically we don't need to erase the source information if all the deduplicated blocks have identical source information, but tracking that seems like more effort than it's worth."

The change targets the kept block's terminator source info (`terminator_mut().source_info`), setting span to `DUMMY_SP` and scope to `OUTERMOST_SOURCE_SCOPE`; it does not remove the unreachable block itself.
Do not claim runtime reproduction or compiler execution; the patch alone was inspected.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct a Rust input that produces multiple deduplicated unreachable MIR blocks with distinct source spans, run it through the SimplifyCfg/MIR pipeline, and inspect the surviving unreachable block's terminator source info. Assert it is `DUMMY_SP`/`OUTERMOST_SOURCE_SCOPE` when deduplication occurred. As a differential check, use a case where no unreachable block is deduplicated and verify its source info is not forcibly erased. A debug-info oriented regression can check that a breakpoint requested on the erased location is not mapped to the surviving unreachable instruction. Inspect the retained test expectation rather than assuming a replacement pass is wrong.
